prompt: What does progressive enhancement mean?
hint: Think of what is still there when the script never arrives.

choices.text: New features ship to a few users before everyone
choices.why: That is a gradual rollout, not this.

choices.text: The page works as plain HTML first, and JavaScript makes it better
choices.why: Right: the base works alone, and the script is added on top.

choices.text: The page loads its JavaScript bit by bit as you scroll
choices.why: That is lazy loading, a different idea.

choices.text: The page asks the visitor to turn JavaScript on
choices.why: The point is the opposite: it works without asking.

prompt: With JavaScript off, why did "Previous week" do nothing?
hint: What kind of element was it, and what made it work?

choices.text: Links never work with JavaScript off
choices.why: Links do work; it was not a link.

choices.text: The week shown was already the earliest week in the data file, so there was nowhere to go
choices.why: There are earlier weeks; the button just had no listener.

choices.text: The server refused the request, because a button may not send anything without a script
choices.why: No request was sent at all.

choices.text: It was a button with an `onclick`, and nobody was listening
choices.why: Right: the handler is JavaScript, and there was none.

prompt: With JavaScript off, "Add session" sent the form with `GET` and an empty query. Why was it empty?
hint: What does a browser use as the key of each field it sends?

choices.text: The inputs had no `name`, and a field without one is not sent
choices.why: Right: the `name` is the key, and there were none.

choices.text: Because the server removed the query
choices.why: The browser sent nothing to remove.

choices.text: Because a `GET` form never sends anything
choices.why: A `GET` form sends its fields in the query.

choices.text: Because the date field was required
choices.why: It was filled, and `required` does not empty a query.

prompt: SvelteKit's name for the server half of a form is a form ___.
hint: Two words in English: form and…

prompt: Why do the planner's changes go through a queue?
hint: Picture two requests that arrive together.

choices.text: Because Node can only open one file at a time
choices.why: Node opens many; the problem is reading old data.

choices.text: So that a failed change is retried until it works
choices.why: Nothing is retried; a failure goes back to its caller.

choices.text: So two requests at once cannot lose a change
choices.why: Right: each change waits for the one before it.

choices.text: To make each change faster
choices.why: Waiting makes nothing faster; it makes it correct.

prompt: Why write `planner.json.new` and then `rename` it, instead of writing `planner.json` directly?
hint: Think of a crash halfway through writing.

choices.text: It keeps a backup of every earlier version of the planner, so a mistake can be undone later
choices.why: The new file takes the old one's place; no copy is kept.

choices.text: It hides the file from the browser
choices.why: `data/` is not served anyway.

choices.text: A crash halfway leaves the old file whole, not half a new one
choices.why: Right: `rename` replaces the file in one step.

choices.text: A rename is the only way Node can write a JSON file that other programs are reading
choices.why: `writeFile` writes JSON; the rename is for safety.

prompt: A new session's id is one more than the largest id. Why not the number of sessions plus one?
hint: What happens to the count when a session is deleted?

choices.text: After a deletion, the count could reuse an id still in use
choices.why: Right: an id must never name two sessions at once.

choices.text: JSON cannot store a count
choices.why: It stores numbers fine.

choices.text: Counting is slower on a long list
choices.why: Both look at every session; speed is not it.

choices.text: Ids must follow the order of the sessions' dates, so a count would put them out of order
choices.why: Ids say nothing about dates.

prompt: Why would the queue not be enough for an application on several servers?
hint: Where does the queue live?

choices.text: Promises do not work across a network
choices.why: True in a sense, but the point is that each process has its own queue.

choices.text: The rename step is not allowed on servers
choices.why: Rename works on servers.

choices.text: Several servers cannot read the same file format
choices.why: The format is not the issue.

choices.text: Each server process would have a queue of its own
choices.why: Right: there is no single place for it, which is what a database gives.

prompt: Where does a page's form action live?
hint: It runs on the server only.

choices.text: In `src/hooks.server.js`, inside the `handle` function that every request passes through first
choices.why: Hooks are lesson 16; actions are per page.

choices.text: In the page's `+page.server.js`, as `actions`
choices.why: Right: an object of functions, beside the page.

choices.text: In the page's `+page.js`
choices.why: That is universal and runs in the browser too.

choices.text: In the component, in its `<script>`, next to the form it answers
choices.why: The component runs in the browser.

prompt: Put Post/Redirect/Get in order, from the button press.
hint: The redirect comes between the two requests.
items: The browser sends the form with `POST`
The browser asks for that address with `GET`
The load functions read the file and the page is rendered
trap: Saving after the redirect would mean the redirect was answered before anything was saved.

prompt: What HTTP status does the action redirect with, so that the browser fetches the new address with `GET`?
hint: See Other.

prompt: Without the redirect, what can reloading the page after adding a session do?
hint: The page on screen is the answer to a `POST`.

choices.text: Send the form again, and save a second copy
choices.why: Right: the browser offers to resend the `POST`.

choices.text: Nothing: a reload always only reads
choices.why: Only a reload of a `GET` only reads.

choices.text: Delete the session just added, since the page is rendered again without it
choices.why: Nothing deletes; the danger is the opposite.

choices.text: Show the default week, where the new session does not appear until the next visit
choices.why: The session is saved; reloading shows it or repeats it.

prompt: Why did the `curl` command send `-H 'Accept: text/html'`?
hint: Who else sends forms to an action?

choices.text: To get past SvelteKit's protection against other sites
choices.why: `Accept` says what comes back, not who may send.

choices.text: `curl` cannot send a form without it
choices.why: `-d` sends the form; `Accept` is about the reply.

choices.text: To ask for a page, as a browser does
choices.why: Right: without it the request looks like SvelteKit's own script.

choices.text: Without it the action does not run
choices.why: It runs either way; only the answer's form changes.

prompt: The browser refuses to send three minutes because of `min="5"`. Why must the action check again?
hint: `curl` did it in the lesson.

choices.text: The browser only checks the fields when JavaScript is on, and the lesson turned it off
choices.why: It checked with JavaScript off too.

choices.text: Any program sends a `POST` without the browser's check
choices.why: Right: minus forty minutes reached the file through `curl`.

choices.text: The browser's message is in the wrong language for some of the people using the planner
choices.why: It is in the person's own language.

choices.text: `min` is usually checked only on number fields that were typed by hand, not on pasted ones
choices.why: The browser checked it; the point is who else can send.

prompt: How is `fail(400, …)` different from `error(404, …)` in an action?
hint: One is returned, one is thrown.

choices.text: They differ only in the status code
choices.why: They show different pages.

choices.text: `fail` redirects to the error page
choices.why: `fail` re-renders the same page.

choices.text: `error` keeps what the person typed, and `fail` throws it away along with the page
choices.why: That is what `fail` is for.

choices.text: `fail` re-renders the page with its data; `error` shows the error page
choices.why: Right: a wrong form is `fail`, a missing course is `error`.

prompt: What status does the lesson's action pass to `fail()` for a form with no valid date?
hint: Bad Request.

prompt: `isDate('2026-02-31')` is false. How does it know?
hint: The pattern alone would accept it.

choices.text: `Date.parse` throws on it
choices.why: It parses it, as the 3rd of March.

choices.text: It keeps a list of how many days each month of the year has, with February checked for leap years
choices.why: No list: it round-trips the date.

choices.text: It writes the parsed date back out and it comes back as `2026-03-03`
choices.why: Right: the same text must come back.

choices.text: The regular expression rejects day 31
choices.why: It only checks the shape of digits.

prompt: Any component can read what the last action returned as `page.___`, from `$app/state`.
hint: Named after what was sent.

prompt: A form sends to the action named `done` with `action="___"`.
hint: A question mark, a slash, the name.

prompt: Why did the `default` action become `add`?
hint: The page now needs a second one.

choices.text: SvelteKit refuses an unnamed action beside named ones
choices.why: Right: so both get names.

choices.text: Only named actions can redirect, and the default one had to answer with a page
choices.why: The default action redirected too.

choices.text: A name makes the action run faster, because SvelteKit can skip looking for the default one
choices.why: Names change nothing about speed.

choices.text: `default` is deprecated in SvelteKit 3
choices.why: It still works on a page with one action.

prompt: Each row's button has the text "Mark done" and the name "Mark done: 24 Oct 2026". Why the longer name?
hint: Think of a screen reader listing the buttons.

choices.text: So that the action knows which session to mark
choices.why: The hidden `id` field tells the action.

choices.text: Otherwise every button would be read as the same "Mark done"
choices.why: Right: the date tells them apart.

choices.text: To hide the button's text from sighted users
choices.why: The visible text stays; the name starts with it.

choices.text: Because `aria-label` is required on every button
choices.why: It is not; the text is usually the name.

prompt: Match each part of a row's form with what it carries.
hint: The hidden inputs are sent and not shown.

pairs.right: What to set, the opposite of now

prompt: Why does the week move into the address, as `?week=`?
hint: What can carry an address?

choices.text: Query strings are often faster than state
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: SvelteKit 3 forbids state in classes
choices.why: It does not; the planner had state until now.

choices.text: The browser stores the query in a cookie
choices.why: It is in the address itself.

choices.text: Links, redirects, reloads and the server all carry it
choices.why: Right: state the person is looking at belongs in the address.

prompt: After the links were added, the address said the 26th and the page said the 19th. Why?
hint: Who was given the data, and how often?

choices.text: The planner kept its own week, copied once from the data
choices.why: Right: two answers to "which week".

choices.text: A link that starts with `?` keeps the old query
choices.why: The address did change.

choices.text: The browser served the old page from its cache, since only the query string had changed
choices.why: It was a client-side navigation with new data.

choices.text: The universal load did not rerun
choices.why: It reran and returned the new week.

prompt: What does the new `Planner` receive instead of the data?
hint: `new Planner(() => data)`.

choices.text: The URL of the current page
choices.why: The week comes from the URL through the load function.

choices.text: A store that subscribes to `page.data` and copies it whenever it changes
choices.why: No store: a plain function.

choices.text: A function that returns the current data
choices.why: Right: every field is derived from what it returns.

choices.text: A copy of the data made with `untrack`
choices.why: That was the old version, which went stale.

prompt: Why is the form's action `?week={planner.week}&/add` and not just `?/add`?
hint: A relative address replaces the query.

choices.text: It tells the redirect which week to use
choices.why: The redirect uses the session's date.

choices.text: Without the week the action cannot save
choices.why: It saves either way.

choices.text: SvelteKit reads the action's name from the start of the query
choices.why: It reads it from the end.

choices.text: `?/add` alone drops the week from the address
choices.why: Right: the week goes in, before the name.

prompt: To keep focus and scroll on a week link, the paragraph carries `data-sveltekit-reset="___"`.
hint: The opposite of true.

prompt: What does `use:enhance` do when JavaScript is on?
hint: Same fields, same address.

choices.text: It moves the action into the browser, so the server is no longer asked anything at all
choices.why: The action stays on the server.

choices.text: It sends the form with `fetch` and applies the answer without a reload
choices.why: Right: the server side does not change at all.

choices.text: It turns the form into a `GET` request
choices.why: It still posts; it only works with `POST`.

choices.text: It validates every field against the action's rules before the form is allowed to leave
choices.why: The browser and the action validate.

prompt: With JavaScript off, what does the `use:enhance` attribute do?
hint: It is code that runs on the element.

choices.text: It shows a warning beside the form that JavaScript is needed before it can be sent
choices.why: Nothing is shown; nothing is needed.

choices.text: It falls back to sending with `GET`
choices.why: The form keeps its `method="POST"`.

choices.text: Nothing: the browser sends the form as the earlier sections did
choices.why: Right: that is the base it enhances.

choices.text: It blocks the form so nothing is sent
choices.why: The form is sent as before.

prompt: Match each answer from an action with what `use:enhance` does with it.
hint: Only one of them leaves the page where it is.

pairs.right: A client-side navigation to its address
Every load reruns, the form is emptied

prompt: With `use:enhance`, adding a session showed which requests in the dev server's terminal? Choose all that apply.
hint: No page was asked for after the first one.

choices.text: A `POST` to `?week=…&/add`
choices.why: Yes: the same fields, sent by a script.

choices.text: A `GET` of `__data.json`
choices.why: Yes: the load functions' data, after the redirect.

choices.text: A `GET` of the whole course page
choices.why: That only happened with JavaScript off.

choices.text: A 303 answered to the browser
choices.why: The redirect came back as JSON, with status 200.

prompt: Why is the button disabled while `sending` is true?
hint: A slow answer, and an impatient finger.

choices.text: So a slow answer cannot become two sessions
choices.why: Right: it cannot be pressed twice.

choices.text: Because the form cannot be sent while focused
choices.why: Focus has nothing to do with it.

choices.text: So that `update()` can run
choices.why: `update()` runs either way.

choices.text: To hide it from screen readers
choices.why: A disabled button is still announced.

prompt: You add a "delete session" button that must work with JavaScript off. What is it?
hint: Like marking a session done.

choices.text: A link to `?delete=7`
choices.why: A `GET` should never change anything.

choices.text: A `POST` form sent to a named action
choices.why: Right: the same shape as `done`, and `use:enhance` on top.

choices.text: A server load that deletes when the page opens
choices.why: Loading must not change data.

choices.text: A button with an `onclick` that calls `fetch`
choices.why: That needs JavaScript.

prompt: Put the lesson's layers in the order they were built.
hint: JavaScript came last.
items: A server function that writes the file
A form action that saves and redirects
trap: Starting with `use:enhance` would build the enhancement before the thing it enhances.
